company.name: Delta Air Lines, Inc.
company.industry: Global passenger and cargo airline, loyalty business, aircraft maintenance provider, and refinery operator [s1]
company.summary: Delta operates a global airline network supported by 1,314 aircraft and served approximately 200 million customers in 2025 [s1]. Its technology agenda now combines a newly unified Digital & Technology organization, a hybrid mainframe-and-cloud estate, and production AI in customer and operational workflows, while high fuel costs and aviation-system disruptions raise the proof threshold for new spending [s6][s13][s14][s20].

overview.whatTheyDo: Delta transports passengers and cargo, sells loyalty economics through SkyMiles and its American Express relationship, operates the Monroe refinery, and provides maintenance, repair, and overhaul services through Delta TechOps [s1].

segments.name: Airline
segments.note: Passenger and cargo air transportation, loyalty-program economics, ancillary services, and Delta TechOps maintenance work.

segments.name: Refinery
segments.note: The Monroe Energy refinery supplies jet fuel and exchanges non-jet products for jet fuel.

trends.trajectory: Delta entered 2026 with broad demand strength and record adjusted March-quarter revenue, then delivered record June-quarter revenue while absorbing its highest quarterly fuel expense [s2][s3][s20]. Premium, corporate, and loyalty demand support growth, but fuel inflation, operational resilience, and constrained aviation infrastructure keep cost and reliability outcomes central [s2][s3][s22].

financials.value: $1.4 billion with a 7.7% adjusted pre-tax margin

industry.trend: IATA cut its 2026 global airline-profit forecast to $23 billion as higher fuel costs and Middle East disruption pressured the sector.
industry.implication: Engineering investments must show direct reliability, revenue, fuel, or operating-efficiency impact rather than broad productivity claims.

industry.trend: The GAO reported that the FAA has struggled for decades to modernize outdated air-traffic-control systems.
industry.implication: Delta's software must absorb external disruption and support faster recovery, making operational resilience and tested fallback behavior high-value engineering outcomes.

industry.trend: IATA says aircraft and engine delays, parts shortages, and workforce gaps continue to affect airline costs and growth.
industry.implication: Data and workflow integration across fleet planning, maintenance, parts, and operations remains a priority, but safety-critical changes require strong evidence and controls.

pressures.evidence: Delta described the June quarter as its highest quarterly fuel expense while affirming full-year guidance.
A court allowed Delta to pursue much of its suit over the July 2024 CrowdStrike outage, which Delta said caused 7,000 flight cancellations.

pressures.pressure: Public and regulatory scrutiny of AI pricing
pressures.evidence: U.S. House lawmakers asked Delta for information about its use of AI in ticket pricing.

catalysts.event: Delta began a beta rollout of Delta Concierge, its AI-powered in-app travel assistant.
catalysts.whyItMatters: The rollout put AI into a customer-facing workflow where reliability, personalization, data access, and escalation behavior are measurable.

catalysts.event: Delta described deployment of AI and automation for bag movement on its Atlanta ramp.
catalysts.whyItMatters: Production AI is now tied to operational performance, creating demand for reliable software, data pipelines, and governed change.

catalysts.event: Delta announced Rahul Samant's retirement and named Amala Duggirala Chief Digital & Technology Officer.
catalysts.whyItMatters: A new executive took responsibility for a combined digital and technology function, creating a current mandate and architecture decision point.

catalysts.event: Delta announced a broad leadership transition, including a new president, chief operating officer, chief financial officer, and chief marketing and product officer.
catalysts.whyItMatters: New operating, financial, and product ownership creates a window to align technology work to reliability, customer, and financial outcomes.

catalysts.event: Delta expanded Delta Concierge to all SkyMiles members.
catalysts.whyItMatters: An AI product moved from selected-user beta to broad availability, increasing the operational, quality, privacy, and change-management surface.

catalysts.event: Delta published Ramnik Bajaj's remit leading the Enterprise Data and AI Office.
catalysts.whyItMatters: A named data and AI owner can sponsor governed AI engineering work alongside the new Chief Digital & Technology Officer.

stack.evidence: Delta's Chief Technology Officer owns cloud transformation, infrastructure, operations and reliability, mainframe, enterprise architecture, and cloud and quality centers of expertise.
IBM describes moving hundreds of Delta workloads and modernizing operations on an open hybrid-cloud architecture built with Red Hat OpenShift.
AWS was selected as Delta's preferred cloud provider under a multi-year agreement; this 2022 source is potentially stale and the current workload split is not public.

stack.technology: Customer, servicing, and employee software estate
stack.evidence: Delta's software-engineering remit includes delta.com, the Fly Delta app, airport customer-service technology, and employee-facing systems.
The Enterprise Data and AI Office oversees enterprise data, analytics, and artificial intelligence.
Delta's AI-powered assistant is broadly available in the Fly Delta app for disruption support, customer-initiated cancellations, bag tracking, and other travel needs.
Delta publicly describes AI and automation in baggage operations at its Atlanta ramp.

patterns.theirEstate: A named software-engineering organization maintains customer-facing, servicing, and employee technology. Repository count, delivery tooling, coding assistant, and queue measures are not public.
Delta runs a named cloud-transformation program while retaining mainframes and has moved hundreds of workloads to an IBM and Red Hat OpenShift hybrid architecture.

Delta has a named CISO responsible for cyber resilience, and the 2024 CrowdStrike incident exposed the operational consequences of third-party software change. No public source quantifies Delta's current vulnerability backlog or patch service levels.

fit.summary: Delta has a very large, software-dependent operating estate, a named hybrid modernization program, a newly unified Digital & Technology mandate, production AI, and unusually visible resilience stakes. The pursuit should start with a bounded non-safety-critical workflow because incumbent platforms, stringent controls, fuel pressure, and the CrowdStrike experience will raise the approval threshold.

rubric.rationale: Delta serves approximately 200 million annual customers, and its software organization spans web, mobile, airport servicing, and employee systems; engineering headcount and repository count are not public.
Delta publicly names a hybrid mainframe-and-cloud estate, cloud transformation, and hundreds of migrated workloads.
Delta operates safety- and time-critical aviation workflows, protects customer information, and has a CISO explicitly accountable for cyber resilience.
A newly appointed Chief Digital & Technology Officer owns a combined function, while the Chief Data Officer leads the Enterprise Data and AI Office and customer and operational AI are in production.
Delta affirmed $3 billion to $4 billion of 2026 free cash flow guidance and has a current executive transition, but record fuel expense increases scrutiny on discretionary programs.

Delta has adopted IBM, Red Hat, and AWS and runs external AI technology, showing willingness to use outside platforms; the CrowdStrike dispute and aviation risk make code and production access harder.

reasonsFor.point: The executive sponsor is new and owns a combined digital and technology function.
reasonsFor.evidence: Amala Duggirala joined as Chief Digital & Technology Officer in 2026 after Delta combined the functions.

reasonsFor.point: The modernization boundary is named rather than hypothetical.
reasonsFor.evidence: Delta's estate combines mainframes, cloud transformation, and hundreds of workloads moved onto a hybrid architecture.

reasonsFor.point: There are customer and operational AI workflows with measurable outcomes.
reasonsFor.evidence: Delta Concierge is broadly available, and Delta uses AI and automation in baggage operations.

reasonsFor.point: Software resilience has board-level business consequences.
reasonsFor.evidence: The CrowdStrike outage litigation concerns 7,000 canceled Delta flights.

reasonsAgainst.point: IBM, Red Hat, and AWS are entrenched platform incumbents.
reasonsAgainst.evidence: Delta has an open hybrid-cloud program with IBM and Red Hat and a multi-year preferred-cloud agreement with AWS.

reasonsAgainst.point: The CrowdStrike outage likely raises the bar for third-party software access and change.
reasonsAgainst.evidence: Delta's litigation attributes 7,000 flight cancellations to the July 2024 outage.

reasonsAgainst.point: Fuel pressure can crowd out an unbounded productivity purchase.
reasonsAgainst.evidence: Delta reported its highest quarterly fuel expense in the June quarter of 2026.

reasonsAgainst.point: AI pricing scrutiny can slow governance approvals.
reasonsAgainst.evidence: Federal lawmakers sought answers from Delta about its use of AI in pricing.

disqualifiers: Delta will not name a bounded non-safety-critical backlog, accountable owner, delivery baseline, and business date.
Security, legal, or architecture cannot approve useful read access to representative code and delivery artifacts.
The incumbent IBM, Red Hat, AWS, or internal workflow already meets the agreed completion, quality, and audit threshold.
No funded route or conditional paid next step exists before technical work begins.

targets.name: Amala Duggirala
targets.title: Executive Vice President and Chief Digital & Technology Officer
targets.scope: Global Digital & Technology, including enterprise technology strategy, architecture modernization, cybersecurity, digital experience, and AI-driven innovation.
targets.tenure: Joined Delta in 2026 after the role was announced on January 6, 2026.
targets.whyStartHere: She has a new, combined mandate and can align engineering modernization, AI, digital product, and governance around one measurable outcome.
targets.opener: As you unify digital and technology, which non-safety-critical backlog is most visibly limiting reliability or customer experience this year?

targets.name: Matt Cincera
targets.title: Senior Vice President, Software Engineering
targets.scope: Customer-facing technology, including delta.com and the Fly Delta app, airport servicing technology, and employee-facing software.
targets.tenure: Current role confirmed on Delta's leadership page as accessed September 24, 2026.
targets.whyStartHere: He owns the engineering organization and can identify a representative backlog, baseline delivery performance, and technical acceptance criteria.
targets.opener: Across customer, servicing, and employee platforms, where could one representative issue prove faster completion without weakening tests, review, or resilience?

targets.name: Narayanan (KK) Krishnakumar
targets.title: Chief Technology Officer
targets.scope: RAISE organization, cloud transformation, infrastructure, operations and reliability, mainframe, enterprise architecture, and cloud and quality centers of expertise.
targets.whyStartHere: He owns the named modernization and reliability boundaries where a governed engineering workflow must fit.
targets.opener: Where does the mainframe-and-cloud boundary still create repetitive engineering work or slow a reliability objective?

targets.tenure: Current remit confirmed on Delta's leadership page published September 15, 2026.
targets.whyStartHere: He can connect AI engineering work to enterprise data controls, model governance, and business-owned outcomes.
targets.opener: Which governed data or AI delivery queue has a measurable business owner but is still constrained by cross-system engineering work?

targets.opener: What code-access, model-routing, identity, logging, retention, and human-approval controls would make a low-blast-radius assessment acceptable?

targets.tenure: Current role confirmed on Delta's leadership page as accessed September 24, 2026.
targets.whyStartHere: She can supply a customer-facing workflow and adoption measure for work in the Fly Delta experience.
targets.opener: Which customer journey still requires too many handoffs or releases to improve, and what customer measure would prove the change mattered?

targets.whyStartHere: As a newly appointed operations owner, he can sponsor a reliability outcome and enforce a low-risk operating boundary.

targets.title: Chief Marketing and Product Officer

targets.opener: Which loyalty or revenue-management workflow has a measurable commercial opportunity but is constrained by delivery speed or system boundaries?

competition.position: Strategic hybrid-cloud modernization and consulting incumbents.
competition.tradeoff: They are better positioned where Delta's workloads, architecture knowledge, delivery teams, and OpenShift operating model already sit.

competition.position: Preferred-cloud incumbent under a multi-year agreement announced in 2022; current scope requires re-verification.
competition.tradeoff: AWS is better positioned for workloads and AI services already operating under Delta's cloud landing zones, identity, procurement, and support controls.

competition.position: Published AI-pricing technology provider in Delta's revenue-management workflow.
competition.tradeoff: Fetcherr is better positioned for airline pricing optimization and already has domain-specific deployment evidence inside Delta.

competition.position: Strong status-quo alternative across software engineering, architecture, data, AI, and reliability.
competition.tradeoff: Internal teams already have production access, aviation context, approved controls, and direct accountability for Delta's customer and operating systems.

competition.position: A visible security incumbent whose relationship with Delta is contested after the 2024 outage.
competition.tradeoff: An incumbent security platform is better positioned for endpoint telemetry and response, but Delta's litigation makes this relationship a caution rather than an uncomplicated advantage.

objections.objection: IBM, Red Hat, and AWS already support our modernization.
objections.response: Treat them as the architecture, not as displacement targets. Test one workflow they do not already complete end to end, and stop if the incumbent path meets Delta's written threshold.

objections.objection: The CrowdStrike outage makes another third-party engineering tool unacceptable.
objections.response: Start read-only on a non-safety-critical repository, document every data and action path, require human approval, prohibit production changes, and let security define the exit conditions.

objections.objection: Airline systems are too safety-critical for an agent.
objections.response: Exclude flight control, dispatch, crew legality, and production operations. Choose a representative low-blast-radius maintenance workflow with existing tests, review, and rollback.

objections.objection: Fuel costs leave no room for a broad platform program.
objections.response: Do not propose a broad program. Use one buyer-owned backlog and one defensible unit, then continue only if accepted work improves without higher defects, review effort, or control risk.

objections.objection: Our internal AI and software teams can build this.
objections.response: Compare against their current workflow on the same issue class. If the internal path meets the agreed completion, quality, audit, and cost threshold, do not add another tool.
